FlashFusion has a product lineage around AI-powered commerce/studio creation and consulting dashboards.
Primary modern implementation direction includes Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, Supabase Postgres, RLS, Edge Functions, and Vercel.
Earlier product variants include Angular SaaS and React waitlist/landing implementations.
FlashFusion AI Assessment App v3.1.0 uses FF Dark design tokens: #0F0618, #1A0A2E, #2D1B4E, #A855F7, #F472B6, #22D3EE, #F8F8F8, #94A3B8.
Business hard rules include $4,500 minimum for any paid audit, proof-of-value as the only free engagement, IP retained by the practice, and no claims beyond verified credentials.
CCA-F / Anthropic certification is pending July 20, 2026; language before that date must be 'preparing for Anthropic certification'.
Notion was removed from canonical architecture because it is experimental and may expire.
Storage context includes OneDrive, Google Drive, GitHub, and local drive; a 2TB drive loss event increased the need for provenance-aware recovery.
Base44 GitHub integration is repository-bound; canonical migration preserves Base44 output while mirroring/deploying to controlled repos.
The platform needs metadata-first, provenance-aware, graph-aware, agent-accessible memory with raw files left in storage and intelligence represented in DB relationships.

Agent architecture includes multi-agent routing, task decomposition, retry handling, context persistence, token budgeting, queue execution, provider fallback, telemetry, audit logs, and structured memory.
inferred: A multi-repo boundary is justified because commerce, agents, consulting, education, and studio surfaces have distinct release risks and audiences.
A monorepo can still be used internally with package boundaries; public/deployable outputs can map to separate repositories.
FlashFusion should prioritize revenue-producing consulting artifacts before speculative studio features.
The fastest path to traction is consulting-led productization: audits, workshops, client dashboards, then reusable agent systems.
assumed: Supabase is the authoritative transactional data store unless replaced by an explicit future decision.
Vercel remains the primary web deployment target for Next.js surfaces.
PostHog, Sentry, Langfuse, and OneUptime are acceptable observability candidates, subject to budget and account availability.
OpenRouter can remain a fallback/model-routing option, but direct provider integrations are preferred for production-critical flows when economical.

architecture_principles: Revenue-first: any schedule/artifact that does not produce action at least twice per month should be paused or reworked.
Claims governance: do not claim certifications, outcomes, metrics, clients, or credentials that are not verified.
IP retained: never concede curriculum, workflow, agent, or template ownership to clients.
RLS-first: every user-visible data path must have database-level policy enforcement.
Metadata-first memory: raw files remain in durable stores; indexed metadata, relationships, provenance, and derived summaries power retrieval.
Agent retrieval is scoped to approved/reviewed context only.
No destructive file moves or cleanup in early reconstruction phases.
